target_customer: Aerospace, defense, marine and heavy industry customers who need lightweight, high-power electric motors, including NASA and the US Air Force
problem: Electric aircraft and other heavy vehicles need motors with far higher power density than available motors, and separate inverters add weight.
business_model: Hardware sales of integrated motor drives plus government and strategic development contracts

founders.name: Jason Sylvestre
education: University of Wisconsin-Madison, MS and BS in electrical engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page. Built electric racecars in college for FSAE.

founders.name: Max Liben
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and CTO in the August 2024 Series A press release and 3DPrint.com. Not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Eric Maciolek
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder and president in the same sources. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: magniX (Magni500)
competitors.what: Electric aircraft motor used by Harbour Air

competitors.name: Magnax
competitors.what: Axial flux motor, about 15 kW/kg peak and 7.5 kW/kg continuous per New Atlas

technical_complexity.rationale: Claimed 13.3 kW/kg continuous for the HPDM-250 integrated motor and inverter using 3D-printed copper stator coils and shared liquid cooling. Claims were simulation-based in 2020, needing dynamometer proof and certification-grade hardware.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending designs and manufacturing know-how, with long qualification cycles with NASA and the Air Force.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Lockheed Martin Ventures invested in 2023 and again in 2024.

market_need_then: ARPA-E's benchmark per New Atlas is above 12 kW/kg continuous for a Boeing 737 class propulsion system, while the best flying motors were around 4 kW/kg. Aircraft electrification was a funded priority.

identity.visual_style: Industrial hardware with Made in the USA emphasis
identity.voice_and_tone: Terse and engineering-led. Tagline: Time to build

branding.community_and_virality: Aerospace and defense press: Aviation Week, FutureFlight, New Atlas, Air Transport News.

brand_strength.rationale: Short tech-style name and a crisp tagline with strong trade press coverage, but name origin is unknown and the brand is niche.

outcome_analysis: H3X is active with 58 staff and products from 30 kW to megawatt class. It shipped drives for customer testing in 2023, won contracts with NASA and the US Air Force, took Lockheed Martin Ventures money in February 2023 and raised a 20M dollar Series A led by Infinite Capital in August 2024. Extreme power density and defense demand carried it, with hardware capital intensity the main risk.
notes: Series A of 20M is stated by PR Newswire (August 6, 2024), 3DPrint.com and others. A February 2023 strategic investment by Lockheed Martin Ventures is reported by AIN and the YC page; a figure that total raised was 9M at that time appears only in search snippets and aggregators (Caplight, kscope), so the round amount is left null. No seed round in 2021 was found. Totals range from 24M to 29.3M. New Atlas (2020-11-10) places H3X in Minneapolis, other sources say Denver or Louisville; the YC page says Denver. Education and employers for Liben and Maciolek not found. Name origin not found. An outcome search found no layoffs or acquisition.
